title: Responses API interop — parity gap inventory, mapping conventions, and rollout roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a minimal, auditable compatibility layer that allows Redwood’s existing Responses-style API and SDKs to interoperate with OpenAI Responses semantics while exposing clear downgrade paths for features we cannot fully match. Scope includes: canonical event/message mapping, streaming chunk semantics, function/tool-calling handshake and side-channel routing, structured output schema translation, and consumer-facing SDK/Docs changes. Deliverables: canonical mapping doc, shim implementation for runtime and SDKs, test corpus and eval harness, telemetry dashboards, and a canary rollout plan.
background: Redwood supports streaming, structured responses, and tool/function calling patterns that differ in event boundaries and metadata from OpenAI Responses. Prior exploratory work in ENG-9157 and ENG-10021 covered adapters and an initial shim; this ticket consolidates gaps into an actionable roadmap. Key constraints: preserve existing latency SLOs, avoid token-count regressions for heavy streaming workloads, and ensure security posture for tool routing remains unchanged.
tasks: Inventory feature parity across Response features: streaming events, message vs delta semantics, function call invocation formats, tool metadata, stop/trim behavior, and provenance fields
Define canonical mapping spec that translates between Redwood internal message model and OpenAI Responses model (event types, timestamps, token deltas, message ids)
Specify streaming protocol shim: wire-format translation for chunked deltas, reconciling message-level 'role' vs token-level deltas, and backpressure behavior
Design function/tool-calling handshake: how to represent function schemas, tool manifests, routing metadata, and accept/reject semantics
Map structured outputs: schemas, validation, and graceful degradation when OpenAI responses use nested arbitrary JSON
Implement runtime shim in serving runtime with toggle flag and telemetry hooks
Add SDK adapters (Python/Node) with fallbacks and migration helpers
Build deterministic test corpus and fuzz harness to exercise partial outputs and error sequences
Canary rollout with 5% customer mirror, monitor regressions, then 25% and full rollout
Author migration guide and changelog entries for customers and internal support
acceptance_criteria: Canonical mapping doc reviewed and approved by API/SDK/Runtime leads
Runtime shim passes end-to-end integration tests covering streaming deltas, function calling success/failure, and structured output cases
No regression in p50/p95 token latency > 10% in dedicated streaming workloads during canary
SDK adapters preserve existing public method signatures and add an opt-in compatibility flag
Telemetry surfaces mismatches and error rates; alerts configured for >0.5% increase in downstream tool call failures
Customer migration guide published and an internal playbook for support
implementation_plan: Week 1: complete gap inventory and produce canonical mapping draft
Week 2: iterate mapping with runtime and SDK owners; finalize streaming wire-format
Week 3: implement runtime shim (feature-flagged) and unit/integration tests
Week 4: SDK adapters and validation tests; internal dogfood on staging
Week 5: canary rollout (5%), monitor for 72 hours; expand to 25% if green
Week 6: full rollout and deprecation timeline for legacy adapter behaviors
rollout_strategy: Feature-flagged runtime + SDK opt-in flag to allow gradual migration
Mirror traffic path for canary customers to compare Redwood-native vs responses-shim outputs
Automated acceptance gates: functional parity tests + perf thresholds before each expansion
Backout plan: toggle flag and fallback routing to Redwood-native model variant with preserved KV cache state
telemetry_and_alerts: Dashboards: per-model/per-route parity discrepancy stream showing mismatched event counts and truncated JSON errors
Alerts: shim_function_call_error_rate > 0.5% over 15m, shim_stream_delta_rate drop > 20% vs baseline
Tracing: correlate shim events with request IDs and downstream tool invocation ids for root-cause analysis
design_decisions: Adopt 'event-first' canonical model where streaming deltas are normalized into 'message:delta' events with explicit offsets
Function calls will be represented as separate 'call.request' and 'call.response' events with idempotent call IDs; tools must echo ids
Structured output translation will favor strict validation with a graceful 'validation_warning' event rather than hard failure when schema diverges
Keep shim logic in the runtime layer (not gateway) to minimize SDK churn; SDKs will provide convenience helpers only
review_feedback: PM (Leah Cho): prioritize unambiguous telemetry so support can route incidents quickly; add customer-facing examples
Design (Ravi Singh): propose UI changes in Console to surface streaming parity mismatches; file follow-up DES ticket
Security (Priya Rao): insist on threat model review for tool-calling metadata; recommend KMS-tagging of tool manifests
Runtime (Ibrahim Khan): flagged potential KV cache invalidation when falling back between variants; added dependency to handle cache warming
